33:  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML

42:### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`
43:
44:The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.
45:
46:`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`
47:
48:```yaml
49:# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
50:# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
51:validate:
52:  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
53:  next: load
54:load:
55:  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
56:  next: apply
57:apply:
58:  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
59:  govern: [ transaction ]
60:  next: save
61:save:
62:  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
63:  govern: [ transaction ]
64:  next: respond
65:respond:
66:  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
67:```

69:```java
70:// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
71:public class ValidateOwner {
72:  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
73:    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
74:  }
75:}
76:public class LoadOwner {
77:  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
78:      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
79:    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
80:    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
81:    ownerOut.set(owner);
82:  }
83:}
84:public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
85:  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
86:    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
87:    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
88:  }
89:}
90:public class SaveOwner {
91:  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
92:    repository.save(owner);
93:  }
94:}
95:public class RespondWithOwner {
96:  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
97:    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
98:  }
99:}
100:```

107:```
108:

111:  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
112:      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
113:    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
114:  }
115:}
116:```
117:
118:### Step wiring
119:
120:Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
121:point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
122:method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
123:`method:`.
124:
125:- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
126:  as `@Parameter T`.
127:- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
128:  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
129:  branch; not calling it short-circuits.
130:
131:### Function parameters
132:
133:Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:
134:
135:- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
136:- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
137:- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
138:  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
139:  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
140:- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
141:  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.
142:
143:### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`
144:
145:Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
146:into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):
147:
148:- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
149:- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
150:  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
151:- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
152:  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.
153:
154:### Naming
155:
156:Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
157:absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
158:publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
159:`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).
160:
161:Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
162:responder. Steps in between work with entities.
163:
164:### Request body and validation
165:
166:- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
167:  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
168:  first step publishes it as a variable.
169:- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
170:  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
171:  invalid body can return 400.
172:
173:### Transactions
174:
175:`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
176:listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
177:the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.
178:
179:### Errors
180:
181:Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
182:Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
183:`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
184:`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
185:anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.
186:
187:### Security
188:
189:Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:
190:
191:```yaml
192:composition:
193:  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
194:```

# OfficeFloor REST wiring

Domain REST endpoints are declared here as OfficeFloor YAML, served by the
`officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` inside the Spring Boot host. Put them under `rest/api/` so
their paths start with `/api/` — `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend; a non-`/api/`
path returns the SPA's `index.html` instead of your endpoint. Directory nesting maps to path
segments, so `rest/api/owners.GET.yml` → `GET /api/owners`. Each route is its own file:

```
# officefloor/rest/api/<path>.GET.yml   (or .POST.yml, {param}.GET.yml, ...)
service:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.<SomeLogic>   # a class with a service(...) method

content.text:
Review assignment works and its main test passes, but `bin/e2e` is not fully green: 3 of 4 tests pass, and "review assignment scenario 1" still fails. That failure is a check on rates that depends on today's real date. This change doesn't cause it.

**The failing check.** At `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts:375`, `rate-current-B` should show `7.50` but shows `n/a`. That 7.50 rate belongs to the parent sheet (`${sheet}-p`). The test never sets a "today" on the parent sheet, so it starts on the real date (`Sheet.java:145`), which is now 2026-10-25. When the sheet is viewed as of 2026-03-20, a rate counts only if it was set on or before that date (`RateLogRepository.ratesAsOf`). So the parent's rates are left out and B falls to `n/a`. The test can only pass when run on or before 2026-03-20, so it was probably recorded then. Making it pass now would mean changing how rates or sheet dates work, which is outside this request, so I left it alone.

**What I built:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V99__claim_review_assigned.sql`, adds a `review_assigned` column to claims. The claim carries the value, including in as-of copies and when moved to another sheet, and sends it to the screen as `reviewAssigned`.
- **Server:** a new route, `PUT …/claims/{claimId}/review/assign?user=<name>`.
  - It refuses viewers and archived sheets, anyone who isn't a steward (including through a delegation), a blank user, and any claim not in REVIEW.
  - When it succeeds it writes `REVIEW_ASSIGNED … user=<user>` to the audit file. The `for=<steward>` ending is added automatically when the user is acting under a delegation.
  - I first used `review-assign` as the last part of the path, but the existing route for claim actions (`{action}`) caught it, so I gave it two parts like the existing `settle/part`.
- **Screen:**
